site_tagline: Recurring patterns across languages, space, and time.
footer_text: Language Patterns — PoC. Cross-linguistic typology and diachrony. Seed data is illustrative; sources to be added.

home_title: Explore how languages share, differ, and change.
home_subtitle: Language Patterns documents recurring strategies, pathways, and cycles across the world's languages — from how unrelated languages express “there is” to how negation rebuilds itself over centuries.
section_geographic_distribution_hint: Each dot is one attested language, coloured by the strategy it uses. Click a dot for the surface form.
section_shared_predicates_hint: Many languages use one predicate for more than one of these three. Each language sits in the region covering everything its predicate can express.
section_column_clusters_hint: Two columns count as close when the same language uses one verb for both. Branches joining further right are the pairs more languages merge; the column order in the grid and on the map follows this tree, so neighbours behave alike.
section_examples_hint: Toggle between Natural / Literal / Gloss to see how each language conceptualises the same idea.
section_neighboring_shifts_hint: Related source–target pairs recorded in the Database of Semantic Shifts (DatSemShift). Unmarked shifts are accepted catalogue entries.
section_comparative_timeline_hint: How expressions overlap, compete, and replace one another across languages. Hover any band for the full date range and note.
section_geographic_distribution_hint_set: Each marker is one attested language, coloured by its evidence set; open it for the expression recorded there.
section_geographic_distribution_hint_ite: Pick one thing, and each dot is how that language says it, coloured by the strategy behind the verb. Click a dot for the form.
atlas_subtitle: Every topic on one map. Pick a pattern or pathway to colour languages by strategy or evidence set, or view all topics at once. In the combined view, marker size shows how many topics attest a language.
tags_subtitle: Tags fall into four facets: the meaning at issue, the machinery that carries it, the process behind it, and how far it reaches.
p_graveyard_description: A sound-change pathway catalogue tracking the disappearance of /p/ across the world's languages.
